defects.problem: a one-time command whose performance the claim itself establishes is recorded as operative
defects.claim_says: 'Section 3 revoked Executive Order 13245 ... on signing, December 23, 2016. The revocation is a completed act whose result continues ... The clause is recorded as continuing'; independent_command_check: 'Section 3's revocation ... was complete on signing'
defects.source_says: Sec. 3: 'Executive Order 13245 ... is hereby revoked.' Owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides), points 1, 2 and 4: where evidence establishes that a one-time command was carried out, record it as exhausted by performance with its best-supported date (here 2016-12-23, from the order's own text), and record the surviving consequence (EO 13245 stays revoked) separately. The claim gives the revocation clause the order's general FVRA predicate as a current basis, which does not show that the clause itself still operates.

defects.problem: a one-time directive whose performance is not established is closed as operative
defects.claim_says: 'no held source shows that the recommendation was made or when ... it is recorded as continuing on the face of the unrevoked order, with the disclosure that its functionally spent date, if any, is not established'; unresolved_material_gaps: []
defects.source_says: Sec. 2(d): 'Within 90 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of Defense shall ... recommend policies to the President ...'. Owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides), points 1, 2 and 4: if whether a one-time command was carried out is not established, the question stays open, and disclosing the gap does not fill it. The claim closes the clause as operative and lists no material gap.
